ketovore.summary: Keto-style very low-carb eating built around meat with a few plants, used to get leaner and less bloated with a simple plate.

quick.overview:
Ketovore is very low-carb eating centred on meat and animal fat, with a small selection of plant foods allowed. People follow it to drop body fat and the puffy, bloated look, with a plate that is easy to plan.

The chain is lower carbohydrate intake, which pushes the liver to make ketone bodies as an alternative fuel, and followers report reduced appetite and less water retention, so the face and midsection look leaner. The name is informal and no trials have tested ketovore itself; the research comes from ketogenic and low-carb diet studies.
quick.how: Most people build meals around beef, eggs, fish and animal fats, then add a few low-carb vegetables or other plants for variety and fibre. It is usually followed as an everyday eating style rather than a short cleanse, and followers commonly report early scale changes within the first weeks as water and appetite shift.
quick.risks: Ketogenic diets can cause constipation, raised blood lipids and kidney stones, and clinical use is medically supervised. Dietetic bodies describe the neighbouring carnivore diet as a fad diet and cite low fibre and higher LDL cholesterol. People with kidney, liver or lipid conditions, or who are pregnant, should check with a clinician first.

angle.text: Ketovore is used for keto-style fat loss with a simple meat-centred plate, aiming for a leaner body and less bloat. Cutting carbs lowers appetite and water retention, which shows up as a slimmer, less puffy look. Research comes from keto and low-carb diets generally, as the hybrid has no trials of its own.

eat-like-a-bodybuilder-rice-chicken-broc.summary: The classic bodybuilding menu of chicken, rice and broccoli: measured protein and carbs that make building muscle or cutting fat simple to track.

quick.overview:
Chicken, rice and broccoli is the traditional bodybuilding plate, eaten in planned portions to build muscle or lose fat. The payoff is a more muscular, leaner physique with very few daily food decisions.

The chain is high protein plus measured carbohydrate, which makes calorie intake easy to control: a surplus with enough protein supports muscle gain alongside training, and a deficit supports fat loss. The three-food menu itself hasn't been trialled, but calorie balance and protein intake are widely covered in sports nutrition.
quick.how: People cook large batches and repeat the same meals across bulking phases (eating above maintenance) and cutting phases (eating below it), adjusting portions of rice and protein. Competitive bodybuilders start cutting roughly 12 to 14 weeks before a contest, and visible changes build over weeks to months alongside lifting.
quick.risks: Risks depend on the amounts and on extreme contest-prep methods such as dehydration. Very repetitive menus can limit variety and be hard to sustain, and individual needs differ, so people with medical conditions or a history of disordered eating may want professional guidance.

angle.text: The rice, chicken and broccoli template is used to gain muscle or cut fat with very few food decisions, building a leaner, more muscular physique. High protein and measured carbs make calorie control easy, and calorie control plus training is what changes body composition. The principles are well studied in sports nutrition; the three-food menu is a convention.

meal-prep.summary: Cooking and portioning meals ahead so calorie and protein targets are easy to hit, supporting steady fat loss or muscle gain.

quick.overview:
Meal prep means planning and cooking meals in advance, often a week at a time, and storing them in portions. Fitness communities use it to hit calorie and protein targets consistently, which supports fat loss or muscle gain and a better physique over time.

The chain is food ready to eat, fewer unplanned choices, and an easier time sticking to a diet. Small studies exist: one six-week group-based program reported better cooking attitudes, behaviours and body composition.
quick.how: People usually cook once or twice a week, portion proteins, carbs and vegetables into containers and keep them in the fridge or freezer. It is combined with any diet pattern, from bulking to cutting, and the benefit builds with consistency over weeks.
quick.risks: Stored cooked food can grow bacteria if kept or reheated improperly, so food-safety storage matters. Some plastic containers can shed microplastics when heated, which is why some people reheat in glass or ceramic.

angle.text: Meal prep helps you hit calorie and protein targets every day, which drives steady fat loss or muscle gain and a better physique over time. Portioned meals cut decision-making and unplanned eating. Small studies link prep programs to better eating habits and body composition.

hot-sauce-thermogenics-spicy-food.summary: Chili, hot sauce and capsaicin supplements used to nudge appetite and energy use toward a slightly leaner body.

quick.overview:
Some dieters add hot sauce, chilies or capsaicin supplements hoping to speed metabolism and trim body fat for a leaner look.

Capsaicin activates the TRPV1 heat receptor on sensory nerves, and proponents say this raises heat production and lowers appetite. Reviews cited on Wikipedia found no direct link between capsaicin and weight loss, and a 2014 meta-analysis reported weak evidence that capsaicin before a meal might slightly reduce intake.
quick.how: People eat spicy food with meals, use hot sauce as a low-calorie flavour, or take capsaicin capsules as a supplement. It is typically an add-on to a calorie-controlled diet, not a standalone method, and any effect reported is small.
quick.risks: Capsaicin can irritate the mouth, stomach, skin and eyes, causing nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or diarrhea at large amounts. Isolated case reports link concentrated pills or extreme spicy challenges to serious events including cardiac problems. People with reflux or ulcers may find it worsens symptoms.

angle.text: Forum posters eat chili and hot sauce, or take capsaicin supplements, to speed metabolism and trim body fat for a leaner look. Capsaicin triggers a heat response that proponents say lifts energy use and curbs appetite. Reviews have found small effects on food intake and no direct link to weight loss.

sea-moss-chlorella-spirulina.summary: Algae gels and powders taken as nutrient-dense superfoods for glowing skin and energy.

quick.overview:
Sea moss (Irish moss), chlorella and spirulina are algae products taken as supplements and added to smoothies, promoted for glowing, healthier-looking skin and energy.

The chain people point to is the nutrient content: protein, minerals and antioxidants, plus carrageenan in sea moss, supporting skin health. The algae's nutrient makeup is documented; the NIH has said evidence is insufficient to recommend spirulina for any human condition, and no studies were found testing these products for appearance.
quick.how: Sea moss is usually blended into a gel and stirred into drinks or food, while chlorella and spirulina come as powders or tablets mixed into smoothies. Users typically take them daily and describe changes over weeks.
quick.risks: Reported concerns include microcystin and heavy-metal contamination of some products, allergic reactions, drug interactions, and high iodine in sea moss. The FDA has issued warning letters over false health claims for chlorella products. People with thyroid conditions or on medication may want to check with a clinician.

angle.text: Sea moss gels and chlorella or spirulina powders are taken as superfoods for glowing skin and energy. People credit their protein, mineral and antioxidant content for healthier-looking skin. The algae's nutrient content is documented, while appearance effects have not been tested in trials.

greens-powders-ag1.summary: A daily mixed powder of vegetables, algae, vitamins and herbs that users take for better skin, digestion and energy.

quick.overview:
Greens powders are blends of vegetables, algae, herbs, vitamins and minerals mixed into water as a daily drink. AG1 is the best-known brand, with roughly 75 ingredients, and users credit it for healthier-looking skin, steadier digestion and energy.

The chain people describe is broad micronutrient and plant intake, better nutrition and gut health, then a visible skin and energy payoff. Supporting trials are small and focus on nutrient status, and no studies were found on appearance outcomes.
quick.how: People mix a scoop into water once a day, usually in the morning, as an all-in-one add-on to their regular diet. AG1 is sold by subscription, often promoted through podcasts and influencers, and users commonly describe a few weeks before judging it.
quick.risks: No specific harms are described in the sources used here. Reported issues are cost, about US$79 per month in 2024, and proprietary-blend labelling that keeps some ingredient amounts undisclosed.

angle.text: Greens powders such as AG1 are taken as a daily all-in-one supplement, with users crediting them for better skin, digestion and energy. The idea is a broad mix of vitamins, greens and herbs improving nutrition and gut health. Brand-supported trials are small and focus on nutrient status.

tapeworm-sanitized-parasite-diet.summary: A fringe weight-loss idea of using a parasite to absorb calories; it carries serious documented infection risks.

quick.overview:
The tapeworm diet is a fringe idea of deliberately ingesting a tapeworm, or a pill said to contain one, to lose weight quickly and get thinner.

The idea is that a parasite absorbs part of the host's nutrient intake, so fewer calories are taken in. No studies were found testing it as a weight-loss method, and it is not an accepted medical treatment.
quick.how: It circulates as a historical and online diet notion, usually described through so-called sanitized parasite pills. Because it is not a recognised treatment, there is no established routine or timeline.
quick.risks: Infection with the pork tapeworm Taenia solium can cause cysticercosis, including cysts in the brain, and the resulting neurocysticercosis is described as the leading cause of seizures worldwide; severe cases can cause death. Treatment also needs medical monitoring. Anyone with a suspected infection should see a clinician.

angle.text: The tapeworm diet is a fringe idea in which people look to a parasite to reduce how many calories they absorb, aiming for rapid weight loss and a thinner body. It is not an accepted medical approach and has not been tested as a weight-loss method.

chewing-and-spitting.summary: Chewing food and spitting it out to avoid calories; in clinical literature it is a documented eating-disorder behaviour.

quick.overview:
Chewing and spitting means chewing food for the taste and spitting it out instead of swallowing. In appearance communities it is mentioned as a way to enjoy food while avoiding its calories and keep weight down.

In clinical literature it is described as a compensatory behaviour in eating disorders such as bulimia: in a 1985 study of 275 patients meeting criteria for bulimia, 64.5 percent reported it. Studies describe patients and examine it as a marker of severity; none tests it as a way to improve appearance.
quick.how: The research describes it as something people do around meals or binge episodes to avoid calorie intake while still experiencing taste. It is documented in clinical settings, not as a routine with a results timeline.
quick.risks: Papers report it as a marker of greater psychopathology and behavioural severity in inpatients with eating disorders, and it has been linked to binge eating. Anyone affected can reach a clinician or an eating-disorder helpline for support.

angle.text: Chewing and spitting appears in appearance communities as a way to taste food while avoiding its calories for a leaner look. In clinical literature it is documented as a behaviour seen in eating disorders and a marker of severity, not as a studied appearance method.

extended-fasting-dopamine-fasts.summary: Multi-day food fasts for rapid weight loss and behavioural dopamine fasts for focus and discipline that support training and sleep habits.

quick.overview:
Two practices share this entry. Multi-day food fasting is used for rapid weight loss and a leaner look, while dopamine fasting, which cuts phone use, gaming and porn, is used for focus and discipline that support habits like training and sleep.

Extended fasting creates a large calorie deficit and shifts the body into ketosis. Dopamine fasting was developed by psychologist Cameron Sepah as a behavioural approach to reduce impulsive behaviour, not literally to lower dopamine; some neuroscientists dispute the idea of a brain reset. No studies were found on appearance outcomes for either.
quick.how: Extended fasts run beyond 24 hours, often 5 to 20 days, usually with water and electrolytes, then a return to eating. Dopamine fasts are typically set blocks of hours or days without screens, games or other stimulating habits.
quick.risks: Prolonged fasting can cause electrolyte loss, gallstones, lean-mass loss and refeeding syndrome, which can be fatal. Dopamine fasting has no specific physical harms reported, though critics call its premise unscientific. Anyone with diabetes, a history of disordered eating, or on medication should get medical advice before a long fast.

angle.text: Extended fasts are used for rapid weight loss and a leaner look, while dopamine fasts, which cut phone use, gaming and porn, are used for focus and discipline that support training and sleep. Food fasting is studied for weight loss; the behavioural version is loosely defined.

alkaline-water-alkaline-diet.summary: Plant-heavy eating and ionized water meant to shift body pH, with followers hoping for clearer skin, energy and less bloat.

quick.overview:
The alkaline diet and alkaline water are based on the idea that what you eat or drink shifts body pH. The diet favours fruit and vegetables and excludes most grains, meat, cheese and eggs, and followers say it brings clearer skin, more energy and less bloat.

Proponents say foods leave acidic or alkaline residues that affect the body. Reviews and physiologists report that diet does not meaningfully change blood pH in healthy people, which is tightly regulated between 7.35 and 7.45, and no appearance studies were found.
quick.how: People eat mainly fruit and vegetables and cut animal foods and grains, and some drink water made with ionizer machines or take alkalizing supplements. Followers typically describe it as a long-term eating style.
quick.risks: Excluding food groups can cause nutrient deficiencies, and cancer organisations caution against relying on it for treatment. Ionizers and supplements add cost, and promoters often sell them.

angle.text: Followers of the alkaline diet and alkaline water say they improve skin, energy and general health by shifting body pH. The diet's emphasis on fruit and vegetables is conventional eating advice, while blood pH is tightly regulated and appearance effects have not been shown in studies.

detox-teas-juice-cleanses.summary: Teas and cleanses taken for a flatter, less bloated midsection and a leaner, clearer-looking face.

quick.overview:
Detox teas and juice cleanses are taken for reduced bloating, a leaner face and midsection, and clearer skin, with the promise of flushing out toxins.

Many teas work as laxatives or diuretics, so people commonly report short-term drops on the scale and less bloat from lost water and gut contents. Published reviews have found no compelling evidence that detox diets remove toxins or help weight beyond short-term loss that is regained, and skin effects are untested.
quick.how: People drink teas daily for a set number of days, or replace meals with juices for one to several days. They are often used before an event or as a kickstart to a diet.
quick.risks: Prolonged fasting can be dangerous, and a kidney injury case was linked to a green-smoothie cleanse. Laxative and diuretic ingredients can cause cramps, dehydration and electrolyte loss. Belief in detox can also delay medical care.

angle.text: Users take detox teas and juice cleanses for a leaner face, less bloating and clearer skin. Laxative or diuretic effects cut water weight and bloat, so short-term scale and midsection changes are commonly reported. Reviews do not support the claim of removing toxins, and skin effects are untested.

fruit-juice-cleanse.summary: A one-to-seven-day juice-only diet used as a reset for quick weight loss, less bloat and a glowing look.

quick.overview:
A fruit juice cleanse means drinking only fruit and vegetable juice for roughly one to seven days. People do it as a reset, hoping for quick weight loss, less bloat and glowing skin.

Eating only juice cuts calories sharply, so short-term weight change is expected. Believers say it clears toxins, but the American Cancer Society and Harvard Health state there is no scientific evidence for the claimed benefits, and reviews report that weight lost is mostly regained afterwards.
quick.how: People replace all solid food with juices, bought or home-pressed, for a few days and then return to normal meals. It is popular online and among celebrities, often before events or as a diet starting point.
quick.risks: Possible dizziness, dehydration and electrolyte disturbance, and metabolic crises in people with undiagnosed diabetes. Long unsupervised fasts can cause deficiencies. People with diabetes or kidney conditions should check with a clinician first.

angle.text: Juice cleanses are done over a few days as a reset, with people hoping for glowing skin, less bloat and quick weight loss. Short-term weight change comes from reduced calories, while the detox and skin claims have no published research behind them.

cold-pressed-oils-olive-oil.summary: Extra virgin olive oil and other cold-pressed oils used in place of refined seed oils, for general health and skin.

quick.overview:
Cold-pressed oils, most prominently extra virgin olive oil, are extracted mechanically without heat or solvents. People in looksmaxxing and diet circles use them in place of refined seed oils, linking them to healthier skin and general health.

The oil is rich in oleic acid and polyphenols. In the US the FDA allows a qualified health claim that limited and not conclusive evidence suggests about two tablespoons daily may reduce coronary heart disease risk when replacing saturated fat; effects on appearance have not been established.
quick.how: People use extra virgin olive oil for dressings, finishing and low-to-medium heat cooking, and swap it in for seed oils. Because its polyphenols are sensitive to heat, light and oxygen, it is usually stored dark and cool.
quick.risks: Few direct risks are reported. Documented concerns involve fraud and mislabelling in the olive oil market, and the FDA claim is described as limited and not conclusive.

angle.text: Looksmaxxers use extra virgin olive oil and other cold-pressed oils in place of refined seed oils, citing skin and general health. Swapping oils changes fatty acid and polyphenol intake, which is the route people credit for healthier skin. Olive oil has regulator-qualified heart-health claims; appearance effects have not been tested.

butter-ghee.summary: Butter and ghee used instead of vegetable oils in ancestral and looksmaxxing diets, linked by followers to skin and hormone support.

quick.overview:
Butter and ghee are dairy fats that ancestral and looksmaxxing diet communities choose over vegetable oils, linking them to skin health, hormone support and a better physique.

Butter is about 80 percent butterfat, and ghee is clarified butter with milk solids removed and a higher smoke point. They supply saturated and monounsaturated fat and vitamin A. Appearance effects have not been studied; a 2016 meta-analysis found small or insignificant associations between about 14 grams of butter a day and mortality or cardiovascular disease.
quick.how: People cook with them, add them to coffee or food, and use ghee for higher-heat cooking in place of seed oils. They are used as part of an everyday eating pattern.
quick.risks: Health bodies advise limiting both for saturated fat: the UK NHS advises eating butter less often, and the WHO's 2023 guidance is cited as recommending plant oils over ghee. Replacing plant oils can raise LDL cholesterol, and ghee applied to newborn umbilical wounds has been linked to neonatal tetanus.

angle.text: Butter and ghee are used in ancestral and looksmaxxing diets as alternatives to vegetable oils, linked by followers to skin health and hormone support through their fat and vitamin A content. Appearance effects have not been studied; guidelines address them mainly through saturated fat.

grass-fed-beef-ethical-sourcing.summary: Pasture-raised beef chosen for a higher omega-3 and CLA profile and ethical sourcing, as protein for muscle and skin.

quick.overview:
Grass-fed beef comes from cattle raised mainly on forage rather than grain. Lifters and appearance-focused eaters choose it as high-quality protein for building muscle, with its nutrient profile and ethical sourcing as added reasons, and some link it to healthier skin.

Reference material reports that grass-fed meat tends to be leaner and to contain more conjugated linoleic acid and omega-3 fatty acids than grain-fed meat. The protein supports muscle through overall intake; appearance benefits specific to grass-fed beef are unstudied, and many health and environmental conclusions are described as inconclusive.
quick.how: People buy it as steaks, mince or other cuts and eat it as a main protein, often several times a week alongside other whole foods. It is usually pricier than grain-finished beef.
quick.risks: No distinct risks are reported. Sources note mixed findings on pathogens and that labelling terms are inconsistently regulated, so products vary.

angle.text: Grass-fed beef is chosen for protein, omega-3 and CLA content and for ethical sourcing as part of eating for muscle and skin. Beef protein supports muscle growth alongside training. Fatty acid differences from grain-fed beef are measured; appearance benefits specific to grass-fed beef are unstudied.

sardines-oily-fish.summary: Cheap oily fish rich in protein, B12 and omega-3, eaten for better-looking skin and general nutrition.

quick.overview:
Sardines are small oily fish eaten fresh, grilled, smoked or canned, valued as an inexpensive source of protein, B12 and omega-3 fats. Some in appearance communities eat them for healthier-looking skin.

The route people point to is omega-3 intake lowering skin inflammation. Canned Pacific sardines provide 375 percent of the daily value of B12 per 100 grams and calcium when eaten with the bones. No clinical studies on sardines for skin were found in the sources reviewed.
quick.how: People eat canned sardines on toast, with rice or in salads, a few times a week as a budget protein. Canned fish is shelf-stable, which makes it easy to keep up.
quick.risks: Sardines are described as lower in mercury than many fish, and canned versions contain notable sodium. Pacific sardine fisheries have faced closures, which can affect supply.

angle.text: Sardines and other oily fish are eaten as a cheap source of omega-3 fats, B12 and protein, with users linking them to healthier-looking skin through lower inflammation. Omega-3 intake is widely studied for health; skin benefits from eating oily fish were not tested in the sources reviewed.

eggs-egg-yolk.summary: A cheap staple of muscle-building diets that supplies complete protein, fat and choline.

quick.overview:
Whole eggs and yolks are a bodybuilding staple, eaten as cheap, complete protein with fat and choline to support muscle gain and a better physique.

The chain runs through overall intake: egg protein scores the maximum on the PDCAAS protein-quality scale, and a hard-boiled egg provides roughly 12.6 g of protein and 294 mg of choline per 100 g. That protein feeds muscle repair and growth alongside training. No published trials were found testing egg yolk specifically for skin, hair or other appearance outcomes.
quick.how: People eat several eggs a day, boiled, scrambled or in omelettes, mixed into meals for protein and calories during bulks or cuts. Cooked egg protein is more bioavailable than raw.
quick.risks: Research on dietary cholesterol is mixed, and several meta-analyses found no association between moderate egg intake and heart disease in the general population. Raw eggs carry a salmonella risk, and egg allergy is common in infants.

angle.text: Eggs and yolks are a staple of bodybuilding and appearance diets as a cheap, complete protein with fat and choline, supporting muscle gain. The protein feeds muscle repair and growth when paired with training and enough calories. Egg protein quality is well documented.

oats-rice-and-chicken-carbs-for-bulking.summary: A cheap staple bulk of oats, rice and chicken eaten in a calorie surplus to fuel training and add muscle.

quick.overview:
A standard bulk built on oats, rice and chicken means eating above maintenance calories with inexpensive carbohydrate and lean-protein staples to add muscle and build a bigger physique.

The chain is a calorie surplus supplying fuel for hard training, with adequate protein supporting muscle growth alongside resistance training. Wikipedia reports a well-established link between positive energy balance and muscle growth; the specific foods have not been trialled as a set.
quick.how: Lifters eat large portions of oats at breakfast and rice with chicken at other meals, raising portions to stay in surplus, and favour slower-digesting carbohydrates. Bulks typically run for months, with muscle added gradually.
quick.risks: Larger surpluses and longer bulks add more body fat, and some lifters report needing a harder cut afterward.

angle.text: Lifters build a bulk around oats, rice and chicken to eat in a calorie surplus affordably and add muscle for a bigger physique. Cheap carbs supply fuel for hard training, and a surplus with enough protein supports growth. The link between positive energy balance and muscle gain is well established.

sweet-potato-carb-timing.summary: Eating carbs such as sweet potato around workouts to refill glycogen, fuel training and speed recovery for muscle gain.

quick.overview:
Carb timing means eating carbohydrates such as sweet potato at set times around training, to fuel sessions and speed recovery in pursuit of more muscle.

Carbohydrates replenish muscle glycogen used in high-intensity exercise, which proponents say supports better training and recovery. A post-exercise anabolic window of about 15 to 45 minutes is described as a suggestion rather than an established fact, and sweet potato specifically has not been studied.
quick.how: People eat a carbohydrate meal before training, during long sessions, or soon after, with sweet potato, rice or oats as common choices. It is usually layered on top of an overall diet that already hits calorie and protein targets.
quick.risks: No specific risks are documented for this practice beyond general dietary considerations.

angle.text: Lifters schedule carbs such as sweet potato around training to fuel sessions and speed recovery, in pursuit of more muscle. Carbs refill muscle glycogen, which supports harder training and recovery. Glycogen replacement after exercise is studied, while the benefit of exact timing for physique is debated.

eating-disorder-adjacent-restriction-thi.summary: Extreme restriction aimed at a gaunt, very lean look, which medical groups treat as eating-disorder risk.

quick.overview:
This entry covers severe restrictive eating aimed at a gaunt or very lean look, often discussed alongside thinspiration (thinspo) imagery and pro-ana content in some online appearance communities.

The route people describe is severe calorie restriction leading to rapid weight loss. Medical organisations such as ANAD, NEDA and the Academy for Eating Disorders have criticised pro-ana content for glamorising illness, and research links exposure to worse mood and body image. It is described in clinical literature rather than studied as an appearance method.
quick.how: No instructional detail is given here. In clinical descriptions the pattern combines severe restriction with appearance-comparison content, and it is treated as a clinical concern rather than a routine.
quick.risks: Medical groups regard restrictive eating of this kind as carrying eating disorder risk, and anorexia nervosa is reported to have among the highest mortality of psychiatric disorders. Support is available through eating disorder helplines and clinicians for anyone affected.

angle.text: Some appearance communities discuss extreme restriction to reach a gaunt or very lean look, often through thinspo content. Severe calorie restriction produces rapid weight loss, and medical groups treat this pattern as eating disorder risk. It is described in clinical literature rather than studied as an appearance method.
